about: Phase 3: the scenarios every voice adapter must pass, in Python (tests/test_conformance.py) and Node (test-conformance.js). Each call is a new caller (a new session) on the same server. A turn: what the caller says, the LLM's reply (pieces, as it streams them), and what must happen. llm / tts: whether the adapter called the LLM / the TTS (null: either). heard: what the caller heard. max_ms: the turn must end within it. saved: every shared answer written, as [question, answer]; never_saved: text no write may contain. server: ok | down | slow (each lookup hangs 2 s) | audio_error (the audio cache fails). aliases: reworded questions the fake server matches to a stored one (a real server matches on meaning; an answer that is a commitment, such as a refund policy, is served only to the same words). concurrent: the calls run that many times at once. understander (v4): the session reads each turn with LLMClassifier and LLMRewriter over a scripted model: for each turn text, the frame it returns (delay_ms: it answers that late) or, as a string, its raw output; a turn not listed gets raw output that is not a frame. real: also run against a real server (CROWKIS_CONFORMANCE_SERVER=1); there a first caller may already be answered from an earlier run (the cache is per tenant), so llm: true is not required, and callers are 1.5 s apart (a new answer becomes findable within about a second).
